what_it_measures: Average annual state-government wage (excl. schools and hospitals), cost-of-living adjusted
source: BLS OEWS May 2024 research estimates (sector 99); BEA Regional Price Parities
unit: USD per year, divided by RPP/100
missing_data_rule: Not applicable (all found). Non-FOUND indicators are dropped and remaining D1 weights rescaled
open_issues: Average wage does not control for occupational mix. D.C. has no ASPEP record, which is why OEWS research file was used

what_it_measures: State-government average pay relative to private-sector average pay in the same state
source: BLS QCEW 2024 (private-sector average annual pay), divided into I1 figure
open_issues: Not cost-of-living adjusted by design (both figures are in-state). A high-wage private economy lowers the score even where government pays well (D.C. scores 2)

what_it_measures: Whether 10th-percentile entry-role wages cover a one-bedroom Fair Market Rent at 30% of income
source: BLS OEWS May 2024 (eligibility interviewers, correctional officers, tax examiners); HUD FY2025 Fair Market Rents, population-weighted to state
unit: Rent as share of cost-adjusted entry wage
transformation_to_0_100: Fixed bar, not a ranking: required income = annual rent / 0.30; score capped at 100 when entry wage clears it
open_issues: Scoring curve below the bar is described in prose only; 21 states sit at the ceiling so the indicator does not separate them

what_it_measures: Three facts: Social Security coverage, plan type, employee contribution rate
source: NASRA Contributions Brief and NASRA plan-type overview
transformation_to_0_100: Sum of points: Social Security covered 40 / partial 20 / none 0; plan type DB 40, hybrid 30, cash balance 30, choice 25, DC 15; employee contribution <=4% 20, <=7% 15, <=10% 10, above 5
missing_data_rule: COULDNT_CHECK for 9 (AR, CA, DC, HI, MA, NY, UT, VT, WA); dropped, other D1 weights rescaled
open_issues: Health insurance and paid leave not measured (no comparable 51-state source). States missing I4 move more under weight changes

what_it_measures: Five-year inflation-adjusted growth in state-government average weekly wage
source: BLS QCEW 2019 and 2024; BLS CPI-U
open_issues: Single five-year window can reflect one budget cycle. Raw value stores two years in one cell

what_it_measures: State workforce turnover rate (higher education excluded)
source: Each state's official HR or workforce report; Reason Foundation as flagged low-confidence fallback
transformation_to_0_100: Percentile rank among states that publish; inverted. Single nationwide ranking
missing_data_rule: Not published: indicator excluded and available Tier C sub-metrics rescaled to the full 65%
open_issues: Definitions differ (voluntary only, total separation, includes retirements, new-hire only, unclear). Percentile makes them scale-comparable, not definition-comparable. Nominal weight: actual share varies by state

what_it_measures: Share of authorized positions vacant
source: Each state's official HR or workforce report
transformation_to_0_100: Percentile rank among states that publish; inverted
open_issues: Rank among 19 publishers is not comparable to a rank among 51; magnitude is discarded

what_it_measures: Mean years of service (medians excluded)
source: Each state's official HR or workforce report
transformation_to_0_100: Percentile rank among states that publish
direction: Higher is better (long tenure can also signal low hiring)
open_issues: Direction is an assumption. Some figures include higher-education staff and are flagged

what_it_measures: How many of the three Tier C metrics the state publishes
source: Same state reports
missing_data_rule: Not applicable. A state with nothing published scores 0 on D2 overall (OH, RI, SC, SD, WV)
open_issues: Mixes 'publishes data' with 'workforce is healthy'. Transparency score is derived from the same availability that drives Tier C coverage, so non-publication is penalized twice (Question 01)

what_it_measures: Favorable trust in state government as an institution, weighted over qualifying polls
source: Statewide polls (13 states; see d3-public-perception/polls.csv)
transformation_to_0_100: Weighted mean of pct_favorable; weight = recency (1.0 for 2024-26, 0.7 for 2022-23) x sample (1.0 n>=800, 0.7 n 400-799, 0.4 smaller or unknown) x directness (1.0 asks about 'state government', 0.6 close proxy)
missing_data_rule: No qualifying poll: P is MISSING and c_P = 0, so D3 reduces to S
open_issues: Proxy for trust in government, not trust in public workers. Question wording differs across polls. Several polls were excluded because the figure could not be verified

what_it_measures: Share of favorable state-government news coverage (neutral counts half)
source: Web search over a fixed 10-query template per state; articles classified by an AI model
missing_data_rule: Not applicable. All 51 have a value; confidence weight c_S = min(1, n_articles / 20)
open_issues: Article-level data not in this repo, so S cannot be re-derived. Search results change over time. Corpus sizes are 8 to 18 articles, so c_S ranges 0.4 to 0.9

what_it_measures: Recognition visibility score
source: n/a
transformation_to_0_100: Not scored. D3 = D3_perception while recognition is pending
open_issues: Methodology allows D3 = 0.70 x perception + 0.30 x recognition once available; whether recognition belongs in D3 or only D5 is open

what_it_measures: Count of distinct statewide PD functions, plus program bonuses
source: Official state .gov pages; National CPM Consortium roster
transformation_to_0_100: Base 0 / 55 / 70 / 85 for 0, 1, 2, 3+ functions; +12 if CPM accredited; +7 if non-CPM certificate program not already counted; capped at 100; floor of 20 only when 0 functions and CPM accredited (applies to CO, MI, TX)
missing_data_rule: Counts what official pages disclose; blocked pages can under-count, giving a conservative 0 (10 states score 0 functions)
open_issues: Measures existence, not funding. 21 states coded CPM accredited, 18 coded 'Program exists' (no credit); expected about 40 accredited, unresolved. Ladder values lack a documented rationale

what_it_measures: Center for Digital Government Digital States Survey grade
source: Center for Digital Government Digital States Survey (via GovTech)
missing_data_rule: D.C. is not surveyed: grade recorded as 'Substitute', no points, D4 left blank and carried as 0 in the composite
open_issues: Measures IT maturity, not investment in people. D4's own rules say never default D.C. to zero, yet the composite does so although D.C. has pd_points of 70

what_it_measures: State law or administrative rule authorizes employee recognition awards
source: State statutes and rules (fetched, quoted)
transformation_to_0_100: 20 points if YES. D5 score = points earned / points possible among checked indicators x 100
missing_data_rule: COULDNT_CHECK removed from denominator. Coverage floor exists in code but is set to 0
open_issues: Near-universal among checked states; low discrimination

what_it_measures: Central HR agency posts a written recognition policy
source: State HR policy pages
open_issues: 17 states could not be checked on this indicator

what_it_measures: Named statewide employee award program with a public web page
source: Award-program pages
open_issues: An old but live page satisfies it

what_it_measures: Published honoree list or documented ceremony or award cycle in last 3 years
source: State pages; news only if the state page is unreachable
open_issues: Overlaps with I6; many states passing both cite the same ceremony

what_it_measures: Proclamation for Public Service Recognition Week (or equivalent) in last 3 years
source: Governor's proclamation archives
open_issues: 13 states could not be checked

what_it_measures: State-sponsored appreciation event beyond the proclamation
source: State pages; news fallback
open_issues: Vermont could not be checked on any indicator, so has no D5 score and is carried as 0 in the composite
